record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Let X be a complex Banach space, T in L(X) a bounded operator, and Y = E_X(T) the linear subspace formed from the generalized kernels of lambda - T, equivalently the union of p(T)^{-1}(0) over all nonzero polynomials p. If Y is dense in X, what can be said about the point spectrum pi(T) = {lambda in C : lambda - T is not injective} and the surjective spectrum pi_prime(T) = {lambda in C : lambda - T is not surjective}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and let $T \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ be a bounded linear operator on $X$. For each $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, let the generalized kernel of $\lambda - T$ be $\bigcup_{n\ge 1}\ker(\lambda-T)^n$, and define
$$E_X(T) = \bigcup_{\lambda \in \mathbb{C}} \bigcup_{n\ge 1}\ker(\lambda-T)^n = \bigcup_{p \in \mathbb{C}[z]\setminus\{0\}} p(T)^{-1}(0),$$
which is a linear subspace of $X$. Define the point spectrum
$$\pi(T) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda - T \text{ is not injective}\}$$
and the surjective spectrum
$$\pi'(T) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda - T \text{ is not surjective}\}.$$
Suppose that $E_X(T)$ is dense in $X$. Determine what can be said about $\pi(T)$ and $\pi'(T)$. In particular, must $\pi'(T) \subseteq \overline{\pi(T)}$, and what further structural conclusions (e.g. on the cardinality, density, or topological structure of $\pi(T)$ inside the spectrum of $T$) follow?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific question concerning operators on a complex Banach space whose union of generalized eigenspaces is dense, and what this forces on the point and surjective spectra. Related results on local spectral theory and isolated points of the surjective spectrum exist, but no source explicitly settling the stated question was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies properties of the surjective spectrum of bounded operators on Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on the surjective spectrum exists but does not resolve the density-of-generalized-kernels question.
